figures.caption: Figure 1: Gradient conflict during multilingual fine-tuning with two base models on eight languages (en, zh, it, ar, ko, id, bn, sw). Left: Mean ± standard deviation of pairwise gradient cosine similarity across all language pairs, with accuracy scores on Global-MMLU dataset. Right: Per-layer frequency of conflicts, defined as the fraction of training steps where at least one language pair exhibits a negative gradient cosine similarity.
Table 1: Main results (Subscripts denote difference from Vanilla SFT).

Figure 2: Illustration of how multi-task update rules handle conflicting objectives. Averaged Gradients risks negative interference by strictly following the mean, potentially degrading one loss to improve another. MGDA finds a common descent direction via the minimum-norm point in the gradients’ convex hull. CAGrad resolves conflicts by optimizing within a trust region bounded around the average gradient. PCGrad neutralizes conflicts by projecting gradients onto the orthogonal planes of competing tasks.

Figure 5: How Bucket-Level MOO affects the internal structure of LLMs. Left: Layer-wise Silhouette scores measuring the representational clustering of languages in Qwen3-8B-Base5. Right: The percentage of language-specific neurons (neurons activated solely by a single language) across different model architectures.
